items.text: Fallen Dragonfly
Field Hospital

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Fabien?
The emaciated young man on the bed lifts his eyelids.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: ... Oh! Paul, it's you!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes, it's ... me. My apologies, it was not my intent to wake you.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: No, no! It's so good to see you, Paul. It's been lonely here, waiting for so long.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The doctors and nurses are busy. It took some time to find your new location.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Them? Hah! They wouldn't do anything even if we howled the place down.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Are we just chunks of meat, waiting to be graded? Old bandages to be tossed aside?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: The people we wait for, the people we love who are waiting for us—no one gives a damn about them.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The doctors can only do so much.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: I know. At least ... I've held on long enough to see you ... and Anna.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Anna ... she came?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Yeah, she was here. The Ginster was withered, but she promised she'd come back with fresh flowers.
A troubled look suddenly shadows his face. After a pause, he speaks his doubts aloud.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: But the doctors say she never came ... I could've sworn I saw the Ginster.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: The little clusters of gold ... Anna placed them on my head and left. Why didn't she say goodbye?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Was it because the doctors took my leg?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No, that is not the reason.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: But they keep saying I'm mad ... that no one's waiting, that no one misses me, no one's looking for me ...

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: So ... maybe Anna didn't come. Maybe she isn't even real at all. I can't stop thinking about it ... It's like my head's splitting in two.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: But I can't stop. It's like I'm not in control of my thoughts anymore—like someone's trying to take over my body.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: It's horrible, Paul, pure horror! I've become one of those madmen we used to joke about! Even my own memories are playing tricks on me!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You're not mad. But you must let your body heal.
Fabien's lips tremble.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: This is worse than death, Paul!
Charon grips the hand Fabien has lifted toward him. Fabien strains to turn his neck to look at him.
His eyes flicker, turning cold and empty.
A chilling premonition creeps up the back of Charon's neck.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: ... Who are you?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I'm Paul, Fabien.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: No.
Slowly but firmly, Fabien pulls his hand away.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: You're not Paul. Paul doesn't talk like that.
For a moment, Charon feels as though he sees a crack at the edge of his vision, but when he blinks, it's gone.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Fabien?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Paul would never say the things you do. He was just a schoolboy—a kid fresh on the battlefield, thrust into this hell.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: No, you're not Paul at all ... but why aren't you Paul?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: ... There's no Paul ... Then, what about Anna?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: No one came for me, did they? No one at all.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Why are you hiding your face, huh? Why are you pretending to be Paul?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There is no pretending, Fabien ... I ... really am Paul.
His feeble words fall upon deaf ears.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Paul didn't come. Anna didn't come. No one came. They want me to die here alone, all of them ...
He sinks back onto the bed, his voice becoming a broken murmur as he surrenders himself to his fate.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: But you came—whoever it is you are. You didn't call me mad ... You didn't tell me Anna isn't real.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: And your words are kind ... Why? Why would you be so kind to a stranger? A dead man?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I do not believe us to be strangers, Fabien. You're not alone.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Yes, I am. Day and night I waited, but no one came. I've been alone all this time, and I'll die alone, too.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: No prayers, no one at my side, just worms ready to wriggle into my body and eat me from the inside out.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No, Fabien. If the end finds you, I ... will be with you when it comes.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: ... What? Even though we're strangers?
Charon tightens his grip on the corner of his notebook.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: When the dead are buried, no prayers leave my lips.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Death is simply the end of life. Prayers are not necessary.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But if it comforts you, if, in your final moments, you need a prayer to be uttered by your side ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... will try to give you the blessing you wish for.
Near the Field Hospital

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I heard your conversation.
Realizing she means the words exchanged beside Fabien's bed, Charon gives a faint nod.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Ah.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: The field hospital's moving back tomorrow. He might survive long enough to get proper treatment back in the rear.
Her gaze is hollow, like she's looking straight through Charon to someone who isn't there.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You've got something to say to me, haven't you?
Everything hinges on tomorrow. Now is "Paul's" final chance to persuade Partita to leave the front.
Charon knows the one thing that might change her mind, but he hasn't had the courage to face it.
But now, the words must be shaped and spoken, clearly and directly.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... A deal. Let's make a deal. You're a person who honors her promises.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I will tell you the truth about Walter's death, and when the hospital withdraws tomorrow, you will return home.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Promises still mean something to you, don't they?
For a moment, time seems to freeze. Then, it steadily ticks on. She studies Charon.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: If you can't even trust me, then who can you trust?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Do you accept? A promise, like when we were children. One you would never break.
A truth too bitter for him to utter. He fears what Partita will do once he tells her.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Alright, it's a deal. I won't break it, I promise.
She senses what's coming but gives nothing away.
Charon clenches his fists, as if summoning the strength to force the words out.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Walter died of friendly fire.
There's a visible crack in her expression.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Who? Why?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: A mistake. The intelligence was delayed and flawed. There was no choice but to call in a strike.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I asked who. Who gave the order?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You swore to keep your word.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I know. Now tell me.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You said you could be trusted.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I said yes, alright?! Now stop dragging this out and tell me who gave the order!
It's the height of summer, yet the air hanging between them is cold.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker.
The frost descends.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Friendly fire is a common pain of war. Sometimes, it is unavoidable.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I don't need you to explain that to me.
She stiffly turns her gaze away.
Charon tries to read her face, but all he sees is a brittle coldness.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Do you still dream, Paul?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No. Since coming to the front, I stopped dreaming of things that cannot be.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I do. I dream of Walter—every single night.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I dream of the pond we used to play at when we were twelve. Walter waits there, hoping to catch a dragonfly for me.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I shout with all my strength, telling him to stop waiting, that the dragonfly will never come. But he can't hear me.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: So he keeps waiting, and I keep shouting, until I wake up with tears on my face.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Then night comes, and I dream it all over again.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Maybe he's waiting for me to find him ... or maybe he wants me to get justice for what happened.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: In war, justice is always the first casualty.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Bullets find their mark, lives end. It is inevitable.
A long silence passes. When she speaks again, her voice is weary.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I need time to think about all of this.
